Notes

Ideas worth keeping.

Find a way in

Worked explanations, practical questions, and a few reflections on making things and leaving room for the rest of life. These pieces are here to be useful or interesting, not to keep up with a publishing schedule.

For an example you can check, start with a working tool versus a trustworthy one. For a different angle, try what makes an explanation feel generous or knowing when to finish.

Tools & technology

A working tool is not the same as a trustworthy one.

Two calculations agree. Both are wrong. A small worked example of the difference between a convincing demonstration and independent evidence.

Decisions & learning

Good decisions, imperfect outcomes.

A fictional gathering, an uncertain forecast, and a $30 choice. Separate the calculation from the people and assumptions it leaves out.

Creative work & communication

What makes an explanation feel generous.

Two versions of the same instruction show how writing can save the reader effort without simplifying away what matters.

Decisions & learning

Learning something difficult from the beginning.

A fractions example, a smaller-week option, and a learning loop that leaves most of the effort for practice rather than planning.

Making things & making room

Finishing is a decision.

Distinguish a necessary repair from another possible improvement, define done, and leave room for the rest of the day.

These are general essays and thinking aids, not a record of private projects or personal experiences. Worked scenarios are labelled as fictional. Research is linked where it is used.

Corrections and substantive revisions are noted on each article. A different perspective is welcome through the contact page. New notes also appear in the RSS feed, with no account or email address required.
